questions.question: You store 'Priya is vegetarian' (January) and 'Priya is now vegan' (March) as two items in a vector store. What goes wrong when you search 'Priya diet'?
options: Nothing; the newer one always scores higher
Both come back with similar scores, and the model has to guess which is current
Neither is found
The vector store merges them automatically
questions.explanation: Similarity search has no notion of 'the current value'. A keyed fact store does.

questions.question: In the fact store, what makes an update replace the old value instead of adding a second fact?
options: A higher similarity score
Facts are keyed by (subject, attribute), so a new value for the same key supersedes the old one
The newer fact is longer
A cron job deletes duplicates
questions.explanation: The key is what turns a pile of statements into a table with one current value per property.

questions.question: An inference says Priya lives in Pune; she told you herself she lives in Mumbai. What does the store do?
options: Overwrites with Pune because it is newer
Rejects the write, because an inferred source cannot overwrite a user-stated fact
Stores both
Deletes the city
questions.explanation: Source rank decides what may overwrite what; newer only wins between equal or stronger sources.

questions.question: What does progressive disclosure mean for procedural memory?
options: Procedures are revealed to the user step by step
Every procedure's one-line description is always in the prompt; a full body is loaded only when the task needs it
Procedures are loaded in alphabetical order
Only one procedure may exist
questions.explanation: The index lets the model know what exists; bodies cost tokens only when used.

questions.question: Your agent knows 60 procedures. Compared with loading all bodies on every call, how does the cost of index + selected body grow as you add procedures?
options: The same way: linearly in the bodies
By one short index line per procedure; body cost stays roughly constant
It doesn't change at all
It shrinks
questions.explanation: That is why skill libraries can grow large without bloating every prompt.

questions.question: A recipe request's prompt includes the customer's phone number from the fact store. What is the right fix?
options: Delete the phone number from memory
Render only the attributes the task needs, e.g. those the selected procedure declares
Encrypt the prompt
Ask the model to ignore it
questions.explanation: Personal data the task doesn't need should not be in the context at all.
